chunks: Aban, from Abdullah ibn Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the Buraaq, which was smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey. It had two vibrating ears, its eyes were in its hooves, and its steps were as far as its eyes could extend. When it ascended a mountain, its forelegs shortened and its hind legs lengthened; and when it descended, its forelegs lengthened and its hind legs shortened. It had a drooping right mane, and two wings behind it.
ai.seo_question: What are the physical characteristics of the Buraaq as described in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi provides a detailed physical description of the Buraaq, emphasizing its unique anatomical features such as vibrating ears and eyes in its hooves, which reflect the miraculous nature of the Prophet's night journey (Al-Isra). In Shia scholarly tradition, this account is often linked to the broader context of the Prophet's ascension (Al-Mi'raj) and the divine appointment of Imam Ali (as) as the gate to the Prophet's knowledge, underscoring the spiritual significance of the journey beyond mere physical travel. The description highlights the Buraaq's adaptability, with its limbs adjusting to terrain, symbolizing the ease with which the Prophet traversed the celestial realms.
